name: Familial Paraganglioma-Pheochromocytoma Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Familial Paraganglioma-Pheochromocytoma Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of pathogenic germline mutation in SDHB, SDHC, SDHD, or other SDHx genes
Presence of multiple paragangliomas and/or pheochromocytomas
First-degree relative with paraganglioma or pheochromocytoma
Diagnosis of paraganglioma or pheochromocytoma before age 40

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of pathogenic SDHx mutation plus at least one paraganglioma or pheochromocytoma tumor
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is critical for confirmation; clinical presentation may vary depending on specific SDHx mutation.

pathognomonic.notes: Episodes of severe hypertension due to catecholamine secretion
searchTerms: high blood pressure from stress hormones

pathognomonic.symptomName: Head and neck paragangliomas presenting as painless neck masses
pathognomonic.notes: Typically carotid body tumors or glomus tumors

pathognomonic.symptomName: Biochemically confirmed elevated plasma or urine metanephrines
searchTerms: high metanephrine levels in blood or urine

common.symptomName: Neck pain or cranial nerve palsies
common.notes: Due to mass effect of head and neck paragangliomas
searchTerms: cranial nerve problems with neck pain

occasional.notes: Resulting from autonomic dysfunction or treatment effects
May occur with malignant or large tumors

rare.notes: Occurs in a minority of cases, especially with SDHB mutations
Due to tumor invasion or compression
searchTerms: nerve problems causing swallowing or voice issues

rare.notes: Rarely associated with paragangliomas producing erythropoietin

laboratory: Elevated plasma free metanephrines and normetanephrines
imaging: MRI or CT showing paragangliomas or pheochromocytomas in head, neck, abdomen, or pelvis
Functional imaging with 123I-MIBG scintigraphy or 68Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT for tumor localization
genetic: Pathogenic germline mutations in SDHB, SDHC, SDHD, SDHA, or SDHAF2 genes
other: Histopathological confirmation of paraganglioma or pheochromocytoma

distinguishingFeatures: Associated with retinal hemangioblastomas, renal cell carcinoma

redFlags: Severe paroxysmal hypertension with hypertensive crises
Rapidly enlarging neck mass with cranial nerve deficits
Family history of paraganglioma or pheochromocytoma
references: Lenders JW, Duh QY, Eisenhofer G, et al. Pheochromocytoma and Paraganglioma: An Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline. J Clin Endocrinol Metab. 2014 Jun;99(6):1915-42.
